_meta.indication: BREXAFEMME is a triterpenoid antifungal indicated for the treatment of adult and post-menarchal pediatric females with vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled; randomized 2:1 to ibrexafungerp 300 mg PO BID x 1 day or matching placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Acute VVC, post-menarchal females ≥12 y (U.S. sites)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure (complete resolution of VVC signs and symptoms) at the Test of Cure visit (Day 11±3)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure 50.5% ibrexafungerp vs 28.6% placebo; P=0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled; randomized 2:1 to ibrexafungerp 300 mg PO BID x 1 day or matching placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Acute VVC, post-menarchal females ≥12 y (U.S. and Bulgaria)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure (complete resolution of VVC signs and symptoms) at the Test of Cure visit (Day 11±3)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure 63.3% ibrexafungerp vs 44.0% placebo; P=0.007

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥2%): diarrhea (16.7% vs 3.3% placebo), nausea (11.9% vs 4.0%), abdominal pain (11.4% vs 5.1%), dizziness (3.3% vs 2.5%), vomiting (2.0% vs 0.7%). No serious adverse reactions; 2 of 545 (0.4%) discontinued.
target_moa: Ibrexafungerp, a triterpenoid antifungal, inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme present in fungal but not human cells, inhibiting formation of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall.
modality: Small molecule (semi-synthetic triterpenoid derivative of the natural product enfumafungin)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; there were no specific issues that needed input from external experts.

description.text: Added new indication for reduction in incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in adult and post-menarchal pediatric females

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of a new indication, for reduction in the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in adult and post-menarchal pediatric females.

summary.text: Ibrexafungerp (BREXAFEMME) was granted Fast Track and QIDP designations for VVC and recurrent VVC in April 2018, and the NDA received Priority Review; it was approved on the first cycle (Review Completion June 1, 2021) based on two placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials, without accelerated approval.

citations.quote: On 18 April 2018 and 19 April 2018, oral ibrexafungerp was granted Fast Track designation and QIDP designation, respectively, for treatment of VVC and recurrent VVC.
The primary evidence of effectiveness of ibrexafungerp for the treatment of postmenarchal females with VVC was provided by two Phase 3 studies, SCY-078-303 (VANISH 303) and SCY-078-306 (VANISH 306).

requirement.text: 4069-1: Worldwide single-arm descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to BREXAFEMME during pregnancy to assess pregnancy/maternal complications and adverse fetal, neonatal, and infant outcomes through at least the first year of life.

citations.quote: **4069-1** Conduct a worldwide single-arm descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to BREXAFEMME (ibrexafungerp) during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4069-2: Perform a milk-only lactation study in lactating women receiving therapeutic doses of BREXAFEMME to assess ibrexafungerp concentrations in breast milk using a validated assay.
